notes: Fitted: sigma_seam from the historical bowled rate, then catch conversion as the historical caught rate over the simulated rate of edges that carry. Fixed at the priors in data/venues.json: e_z (assumptions inside the literature range 0.46 to 0.65, ADR-006) and sigma_swing. Two rates cannot identify more than two parameters.

Catch conversion range, wicketkeeper catches only to all catches: 0.290 to 0.734 at lords, 0.079 to 0.181 at perth, 0.166 to 0.474 at newlands. The shipped value is the upper end, because all catches are an upper bound on cordon catches; the lower end counts only catches by the innings' wicketkeeper, identified by the stumping proxy in data/calibration_moments.json. sigma_seam is the same at both ends, because the bowled target is.

Fitted values are effective values for this outcome model, not measurements. Catch conversion absorbs everything between an edge that the model says carries and a catch in the scorebook: edges that fly wide of the cordon or fall between catchers, drops, and any excess of edges in the model itself.
Synthetic study, 9 fits with sigma_swing and e_z held at the truth: sigma_seam came back within 10% in 9 and catch conversion in 8; errors -4% to +1% and -1% to +10%.

Synthetic study, e_z held 0.05 from the truth (less where that would leave the 0.46 to 0.65 range): too low moves sigma_seam -19% to -1% and catch conversion +54% to +181%; too high moves them +5% to +21% and -50% to -10%. A catch conversion clamped at 1 understates the first range. The fitted values are conditional on the e_z priors, which are assumptions.
Synthetic study, sigma_swing held 50% from the truth: too low moves sigma_seam +1% to +11% and catch conversion -27% to -4%; too high moves them -12% to -2% and +9% to +51%.

Synthetic study, the exact fit ignoring the leave rule (every delivery played): sigma_seam moves -4% to +1% and catch conversion -49% to -30%. Left deliveries are almost never bowled, so the bowled rate and sigma_seam barely change. Playing them adds edges that the batter never offered, so the simulated rate of carrying edges is too high and catch conversion comes back too low.

runs_middled is not fitted. Per venue it is historical batter runs per legal ball divided by the simulated share of deliveries that are played and middled, so simulated runs per ball equal history by construction. The top-level runs_middled is the mean across venues.

Leave rule: the batter leaves when the expected arrival at the bat is more than 0.3 m outside off stump. The threshold is an assumption that cannot be fitted without line and action data (ADR-010); each venue's simulated.left is the share of deliveries left under it, and simulated.false_shot_share_of_played is the share of played deliveries edged or missed.

Simulated population: right-arm over the wicket to a right-hander with the engine's default ReleaseSpec, ball ages 3, 8, 13, 18, 23 and both bowling ends in equal parts, 200,000 deliveries per evaluation, fixed seeds (common random numbers). Left-armers, left-handers and spin are not simulated.
Historical rates are per legal ball in overs 1 to 25 of men's Tests, all bowlers and batters. Dismissals outside the model (ADR-007) are not wickets for these rates but their balls count.

Intervals are 95% percentile intervals over 200 bootstrap resamples of each venue's ball outcomes (bowled, caught or neither). They cover sampling noise in the historical counts only: balls are treated as independent, and e_z, sigma_swing, the leave rule, the release population and the choice of catch target are held fixed.
rejected_two_parameter_fit is the first parameterisation (sigma_seam and e_z fitted, every carrying edge caught), kept for the record with the reason it was rejected.
